footer.blurb: A social network built to stress-test Ultimate: every primitive, once, in one real app. Public pages here ship no JavaScript at all.
footer.seeded: Seeded demo data. Every account, post and photo here is fabricated.

actions.none: No action on this resource is available to you.

denied.body: Refused. {permission} was not granted to this actor ({reason}). The same decision declines to render the control and refuses the call behind it.

users.title: People
users.description: Every account in the demo, generated from the users entity.

posts.title: Posts
posts.description: Published posts. A soft-deleted row is hidden by the entity, not by a filter here.

media.title: Uploads
media.description: Uploaded bytes and the state the hourly sweep acts on.

jobs.title: Jobs
jobs.description: What the queue can run, with the retry policy each job declares.
jobs.name: Job

ops.title: Operations
ops.description: The demo's scheduled work and the uploads it acts on.
ops.uploadsHint: An upload that never gets claimed is collected by the hourly sweep and moved to orphan.
ops.scheduleHint: Every cron carries an explicit IANA zone. An unzoned cron runs twice or not at all on a DST switch day.

dashboard.description: Four screens, four policies. Nothing on this page is readable without the permission the route declares — including this page.
dashboard.title: Dashboard

friends.title: Friends
friends.body: Who asked whom, in five lists — because direction is part of the fact.

messages.title: Messages
messages.body: A row in participants is permission to read a thread. There is no second grant.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.body: Unread is derived from readAt, so marking read is safe to replay offline.

feed.title: Public feed
feed.body: The same list a signed-out reader gets, decided by the same policy object.

friends.title: Friends
friends.description: Who asked whom is part of the fact, so a request you sent and a request you received are two different lists.

incoming.title: Incoming requests
incoming.description: People who asked to be your friend. Only you can answer these.
incoming.empty: Nobody is waiting on an answer from you.

outgoing.title: Sent requests
outgoing.description: People you asked. You cannot answer your own request.
outgoing.empty: You have no requests waiting on an answer.

current.title: Friends
current.description: Accepted in either direction. A friends-only post is visible to exactly these people.

declined.title: Declined
declined.description: Answered with a no, in either direction. The row stays so the pair can never grow a second one.

blocked.title: Blocked by you
blocked.description: Neither of you sees the other's posts. A block someone else placed is deliberately not listed here.

messages.title: Messages
messages.description: A row in participants is permission to read a thread. There is no second grant to keep in step.
messages.emptyHelp: Membership is the only grant, so a thread you were never added to is not listed and not readable — the same answer a conversation that does not exist gives.
messages.noMessages: Nothing sent in this thread yet.

thread.title: Thread
thread.emptyHelp: Messages appear newest first, ordered by (createdAt desc, id) — the tail key is what makes the order total.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Unread is derived from readAt, never stored and never decremented — which is what makes marking read safe to replay offline.
notifications.emptyHelp: Sending a message writes one notification per other participant, so this fills up as soon as somebody writes to you.

offline.description: This page will refresh itself when the connection returns.
offline.title: You are offline
offline.help: Every app/ route declares its own offline strategy, and the service worker is generated from those declarations rather than hand-written.

home.title: A social network, built to break a framework
home.description: Every Ultimate primitive, once, in one real app: relational visibility decided by a policy, a live feed, offline reads, uploads and an admin that shares the same authz object as the API.
home.eyebrow: This page ships 0 kb of JavaScript
home.seeded: Seeded demo data. Every account, post and photo here is fabricated.

decision.caption: What a signed-out reader may see
decision.note: Not a WHERE clause. One policy object answers the HTTP route, the live query, the MCP tool and the admin button — and it is re-decided per row, per subscriber.

primitives.label: primitives, and the list is closed

authz.label: policy object per decision, on all four surfaces

declaration.title: None of that is configuration. It is a declaration.
declaration.body: A route says how it renders, whether it hydrates, what it does offline and what it may cost. The service worker, the budget check and the prerender list are all generated from those five lines — so a page cannot quietly start shipping JavaScript.

point.one: The directory is the URL. There is no route table to keep in step.
point.two: A budget is a build failure, not a note in a README.
point.three: Who may read a post is one policy object, asked by HTTP, live queries, the MCP tools and the admin alike.

closing.title: Everything here is real, and none of it is true
closing.body: The data is fabricated and the app is not. Read the feed and every row you see was decided by a policy, not by a WHERE clause.

proofs.title: What this deployment is evidence for

policy.title: One authz object, four surfaces
policy.body: Who may see a post is friendship and blocks, not a tenant column — and the HTTP route, the live query, the MCP tool and the admin button all ask the same policy.

realtime.title: Live queries, not polling
realtime.body: A read declared live: true becomes a subscription, with the row gate re-decided per subscriber.

offline.title: Offline is a route declaration
offline.body: Each route says precache, runtime or network-only, and the service worker is generated from the route table.

admin.title: Admin is view-only by permission
admin.body: It holds admin:read and never admin:write. One decision renders the button and answers the call.

feed.title: The public feed
feed.description: Everything here is seeded and fake. What you can see is decided by a policy, not by a WHERE clause.
feed.emptyHelp: Every post the seed created is either friends-only, private, or written by someone who blocked the demo user — so a signed-out reader is shown none of them.

profile.title: {name} (@{handle})
profile.description: {name} on SocialMediaClone. Everything here is seeded and fake.

posts.title: Posts
posts.empty: Nothing here that a signed-out reader may see
posts.emptyHelp: This account may have posted plenty. A friends-only post, a private note and a soft-deleted row are all absent without a WHERE clause saying so.

notFound.title: No such profile
notFound.description: There is no account with that handle. Handles are lowercase, and a URL differing only in case is a different URL.

signin.title: Sign in
signin.description: Two seeded demo accounts, and a session cookie whose token is stored hashed.
signin.captchaOff: No hCaptcha keys are set, so no challenge is rendered and none is demanded. Set HCAPTCHA_SITE_KEY and HCAPTCHA_SECRET to turn it on.
signin.captchaAfterFailures: After {count} refusals for one handle, this form demands the challenge before it checks the password.

demo.title: The two demo accounts
demo.admin: admin / admin — read-only operator, by permission rather than by hidden buttons.

signOut.title: Sign out
signOut.description: Clears the session cookie on this browser.

signup.title: Create an account
signup.description: Every sign-up is challenged when hCaptcha keys are configured — account creation is what a bot is here for.
signup.handleHint: Lowercase letters, digits and underscores. This is your URL.
